Analisi dell’indice di innovazione per CAP

Marco

2025-04-10

data <- read_delim("innoidx_finfrm.csv", 
                             delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE, 
                             trim_ws = TRUE, show_col_types = FALSE)
colnames(data)[9] <- "pred_inno"
data_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(postcode_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_pred = mean(pred_inno, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_pred = ifelse(n() > 1, sd(pred_inno, na.rm = TRUE), NA),
    SE = ifelse(n() > 1, sd_pred / sqrt(n), NA),
    CI_lower = ifelse(n() > 1, mean_pred - qt(0.975, df = n()-1)*SE, NA),
    CI_upper = ifelse(n() > 1, mean_pred + qt(0.975, df = n()-1)*SE, NA),
    CI_width = ifelse(n() > 1, (CI_upper - CI_lower), NA),
    median_pred = median(pred_inno, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
print(data_summary)

data_filtered <- data_summary
print(data_filtered)

# Calcola gli estremi per posizionare le annotazioni
xrange <- range(data_filtered$mean_pred, na.rm = TRUE)
yrange <- range(data_filtered$median_pred, na.rm = TRUE)

# Definisce le coordinate per l'annotazione:
# Nel triangolo in alto (dove median > mean, left skewed)
left_x <- xrange[1] + 0.3 * diff(xrange)
left_y <- yrange[1] + 0.8 * diff(yrange)
# Nel triangolo in basso a destra (dove mean > median, right skewed)
right_x <- xrange[1] + 0.8 * diff(xrange)
right_y <- yrange[1] + 0.3 * diff(yrange)
grid_data <- expand.grid(mean_pred = seq(0, 1, length.out = 100),
                         median_pred = seq(0, 1, length.out = 100))
grid_data$I <- with(grid_data, (mean_pred^0.5) * (median_pred^0.5))

data_filtered <- data_filtered %>%
  mutate(color_group = case_when(
    grepl("^201", postcode_id) ~ "milano",
    grepl("^411", postcode_id) ~ "modena",
    TRUE ~ "Altri CAP"
  ),
  alpha_value = ifelse(color_group == "Altri CAP", 0.1, 1))

p2 <- ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = mean_pred, y = median_pred)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = color_group), size = 2.5, alpha = data_filtered$alpha_value) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("milano" = "yellow", "modena" = "green", "Altri CAP" = "darkred")) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_contour(data = grid_data, aes(z = I), bins = 10, colour = "black") +
  geom_text_contour(data = grid_data, aes(z = I), bins = 10, stroke = 0.2, size = 3.5) +
  annotate("text", x = left_x, y = left_y, label = "left skewed area", size = 5) +
  annotate("text", x = right_x, y = right_y, label = "right skewed area", size = 5) +
  labs(title = "Scatter plot: Media vs Mediana con curve di livello",
       x = "Media di pred_inno",
       y = "Mediana di pred_inno",
       color = "Gruppo CAP") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p2)

Il grafico rappresenta i posibili valori di media e mediana (tra 0 e 1). le cruve di livello i valori dell’indice. A nord-est della bisettrice abbiamo CAP per cui la mediana è maggiore della media. A sud-ovest i casi complemntari. Ogni puntino rappresent un cap. Alcuni solo colorati secondo l’indice.

data_filtered <- data_filtered %>%
  mutate(color_group = factor(ifelse(n < 20, "n < 20", "n ≥ 20"), levels = c("n < 20", "n ≥ 20")))

p4 <- ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = n)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribuzione della variabile n",
       x = "Numero osservazioni (n)",
       y = "Frequenza") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p4)

ATTENZIONE. tansissimi cap con poche imprese.

data_filtered$index <- (data_filtered$mean_pred^0.5) * (data_filtered$median_pred^0.5)

p3 <- ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = index)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribuzione dell'indice",
       x = "Indice",
       y = "Frequenza") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p3)

p6 <- ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = n, y = index)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = color_group), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Scatter plot: index vs. numerosità",
       x = "Numero osservazioni",
       y = "Indice",
       color = "CAP") +
  theme_minimal()
print(p6)

Attenzione la maggior parte dei cap con valore molto alto sono cap con pochissime osservazioni.

shapefile_path <- "innoidx_cap.shp"
cap_shapes <- st_read(shapefile_path)
## Reading layer `innoidx_cap' from data source 
##   `C:\Users\MG_48070354\Desktop\inno_cap\innoidx_cap.shp' using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
## Simple feature collection with 8778 features and 17 fields
## Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
## Dimension:     XY
## Bounding box:  xmin: 6.62665 ymin: 35.49308 xmax: 18.52028 ymax: 47.092
## Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
colnames(data_filtered)[1] <- "CAP"
cap_shapes_joined <- cap_shapes %>%
  left_join(data_filtered, by = "CAP")

cap_shapes_joined$index_cat <- cut(cap_shapes_joined$index,
                                   breaks = c(0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.7, 1),
                                   include.lowest = TRUE,
                                   right = TRUE,
                                   labels = c("0-0.3", "0.3-0.6", "0.6-0.7", "0.7-1"))

mappa <- ggplot(cap_shapes_joined) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = index_cat), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(title = "Mappa dei CAP: indice",
       fill = "Indice") +
  theme_minimal()
print(mappa)

mappa <- ggplot(cap_shapes_joined %>% filter(n > 50)) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = index), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(title = "Mappa dei CAP: indice (n > 50)",
       fill = "Indice") +
  theme_minimal()
print(mappa)
